APCTT-C01.quote: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers one-dimensional step-backwater Hydrologic Engineering Center River Analysis System model (HEC–RAS), was used to compute the water-surface profiles along the study reach.
APCTT-C01.note: Basis: one-dimensional step-backwater hydraulics; flood-frequency analysis with the Benson regulation criterion (p14).

APCTT-C02.quote: The purpose of the flood-recovery maps is to provide local government and citizens with accurate and up-to-date information on flood hazards to aid in the rebuilding process.
APCTT-C02.note: Application for recovery and flood response, linked to the streamgage stage.

APCTT-C03.quote: Based on the hydraulic models, Tropical Storm Irene water-surface elevations exceeded the 1-percent AEP flood throughout the 8.3-mile study reach.
APCTT-C03.note: Model results for the study reach.

APCTT-C05.quote: One of the differences exceeds 1 ft; however, the results demonstrate that the model is capable of simulating accurate water levels.
APCTT-C05.note: Model calibrated to Tropical Storm Irene high-water marks in the reach (p15).

APCTT-C06.quote: A series of digital flood-recovery maps and flood-inundation maps were developed by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) in cooperation with the Federal Emergency Management Agency for the Winooski River in Waterbury, Vermont.
APCTT-C06.note: Maps produced for the real 8.3-mile reach.

APCTT-C07.quote: These flood inundation maps can be accessed through the USGS Flood Inundation Mapping Science Web site (http://water.usgs.gov/ osw/flood_inundation/).
APCTT-C07.note: Maps served in the Flood Inundation Mapper, linked to the real-time streamgage and the NWS AHPS forecast (p18).

APCTT-C08.note: Maps are advisory and not for regulatory use (p13, p18); no qualification.

APCTT-C09.note: No record of use over a period.

APCTT-C10.quote: The vertical accuracy of the data meets or exceeds the 18.13-centimeter vertical accuracy standard at the 95-percent confidence level with the result that all areas along the study reach with flood-ing potential are covered by a high-resolution DEM.
APCTT-C10.note: Borderline: a stated accuracy standard and whether it was met, for the elevation data used by the maps.

APCTT-C11.quote: Normal depth was used as the starting water surface and was based on an estimated average water-surface slope of 0.0021 foot per foot of distance for the Winooski River using data contained in the effective flood insurance study (Federal Emergency Management Agency, 2013) and channel survey data.
APCTT-C11.note: Boundary conditions, surveys (p16) and discharges used.

APCTT-C12.quote: The maps are based on simulated water-surface profiles from hydraulic models developed using the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ HEC–RAS and HEC–GeoRAS computer programs.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the Winooski flood maps themselves.

notes: Agrees with the organizer estimate TRL 7.
